title: Black Light FTL Coupled Subsystem Degradation and Power/Thermal Transient Registry
purpose: Model deterministic common-cause degradation across sensing, navigation, computation, actuation, exit, recovery, thermal and structural safety channels without treating those channels as statistically independent and without inventing failure probabilities.

designIntentSource.title: The different lightspeed methods
designIntentSource.scope: Sensor lookahead, emergency de-transit, increasing but imperfect safety margins, gravity-sensitive failure, and physically defensible mathematical underlays.

mathematicalModel.thermalLumpedCapacity: dT/dt = (P_heat - P_reject)/C_th; for constant powers over a short horizon, T(t) = T0 + (P_heat-P_reject)t/C_th
mathematicalModel.aggregationReason: MAX_ENVELOPE is deterministic and deliberately avoids multiplying correlated subsystem penalties as if they were independent probabilities.
mathematicalModel.interpretation: Shared infrastructure can reduce several safety functions simultaneously. The model changes installation readiness and timing authority only; it does not change G, the external tidal tensor, transit-family identity, or fictional hazard existence.

profiles.canonPolicy: Coefficients are versioned engineering calibration, not universal physical constants or historical canon. A narrower named profile may replace them when sourced.

signatureImplications: bus sag or converter current rise

raceAndTechnologyEmbodiments.canonGuard: Ar'nock embodiment does not establish an FTL family or canonical coupling coefficients. Use measured readiness or explicitly labeled simulation calibration.

sharedInfrastructure: Forward Sensor Ampulla and Sensor Choir
failureLinks: cooling loss can degrade solver, actuator and recovery margins together
hydraulic or dielectric degradation can produce asymmetric vane response
power-fluid depletion can reduce actuation and protected recovery authority simultaneously
raceAndTechnologyEmbodiments.canonGuard: The source phrase gravitic slipstream remains unresolved against consolidated FTL family IDs. Machinery coupling does not select a family by keyword.

runtimeRules: Use measured transient state when supplied; do not invent temperatures, powers, flows, buffer energy or probabilities.
A named sourced profile outranks the generic proposed profile; equal-precedence conflicting profiles return CONFLICT.
MAX_ENVELOPE is the default correlated-stress aggregation and must not be reinterpreted as a probability model.

Temperature at or above a declared equipment limit, or power-hold time shorter than a declared intervention horizon, may block affected channels when the caller explicitly supplies those limits/horizons.
Missing transient telemetry preserves the incoming readiness rather than guessing degradation.
Coupled degradation can only preserve or reduce incoming readiness unless a separately sourced repair/calibration authority explicitly improves the baseline.
External spacetime mathematics and fictional hazard canon remain upstream and unchanged.
canonGuards: No coupling coefficient is a historical fact unless a named source explicitly establishes it.
No failure probability is inferred from readiness or stress values.
A thermal or power transient is evidence about machinery condition, not evidence that a fictional FTL hazard exists.
Race/species identity constrains embodiment only and never creates family identity or universal performance canon.
